title: Elon Musk say Tesla is working to prevent robotaxis from running over gray cats on the road
key_facts: On Saturday 3 Oct 2026 Musk said on X that Tesla is extending robotaxi operating hours in Austin from 10 p.m. to 11 p.m.
He said the main problem the team is solving is avoiding pets that are hard to see at night, 'grey kittens on grey tarmac in the dark'.
Tesla robotaxis navigate with cameras and sensors, no lidar; Tesla's own manuals say low light can limit camera accuracy.
Musk said AI 'photon count analysis' lets cameras see well in the dark.
NHTSA is investigating Tesla's camera-based Full Self-Driving system over hazard detection in poor visibility.
In September 2025 a Tesla Model Y in the Austin robotaxi service struck a dog, which ran off apparently uninjured, per Tesla's NHTSA filing.
Waymo, which uses lidar, struck and killed a cat named KitKat in San Francisco last year.
quote_evidence: "The main thing we're trying to solve is making sure that we don't run over pets when they're hard to see at night," Musk wrote in an X post.
The Tesla CEO announced on Saturday that the company is expanding the operating hours of its robotaxis from 10 p.m. to 11 p.m. in Austin

The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration is investigating Telsa's camera system for full self-driving vehicles and whether it's good enough at spotting road hazards in less-than-ideal visibility conditions.
why_it_matters_hint: Night driving is the open question for Tesla's camera-only robotaxis, and Musk himself names it as the thing holding back later hours.
notes: Single outlet reporting Musk's own X posts; no independent check of Tesla's night performance.
